precepts.text: Sarah laughs within herself at the promise of a son because she and Abraham are old, and the Lord asks whether anything is too hard for him.
precepts.point: Gehazi tells Elisha the woman has no child and her husband is old. Elisha tells her that about this season, according to the time of life, she shall embrace a son. Like our mother Sarah, she does not believe it and tells the man of God not to lie to his handmaid, yet she conceives and bears a son at that season.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

precepts.why:
Abraham and Sarah “were old and well stricken in age”, and “Sarah laughed within herself, saying, After I am waxed old shall I have pleasure, my lord being old also?” The Lord answered, “Is any thing too hard for the Lord? At the time appointed I will return unto thee, according to the time of life, and Sarah shall have a son.”

The Shunammite stands where our mother Sarah stood. She was a great woman who fed the man of God and made him a little chamber on the wall, and Elisha wanted to bless her: “thou hast been careful for us with all this care; what is to be done for thee?” She had no child, and her husband was old. When Elisha told her, “About this season, according to the time of life, thou shalt embrace a son”, she did not believe it, just like Sarah: “Nay, my lord, thou man of God, do not lie unto thine handmaid.” The same words, “according to the time of life”, are in both promises.

And the same answer holds: nothing is too hard for the Lord. Sarah had her son, and “the woman conceived, and bare a son at that season that Elisha had said unto her, according to the time of life.”

points: A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cries to Elisha that her husband is dead, that her husband feared the Lord, and that the creditor has come to take her two sons to be bondmen. Because the husband died in debt, the creditor comes to take the sons to work off what is owed.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha asks what she has in the house, and she says nothing but a pot of oil. He tells her to borrow empty vessels from all her neighbors, not a few, then shut the door upon herself and her sons and pour oil into all the vessels.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: She pours out, and the oil continues until every vessel is full, and only then does the oil stay. Elisha tells her to sell the oil, pay her debt, and live with her children on the rest. The empty vessels she borrowed from her people, the children of Israel, were filled through the spirit of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha passes through Shunem, where a great woman constrains him to eat bread, and as often as he passes by he turns in there to eat. She perceives that he is a holy man of God and tells her husband to make a little chamber on the wall with a bed, a table, a stool, and a candlestick, so he may turn in whenever he comes.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: On a day when he rests in the chamber, Elisha wants to bless her and sends Gehazi to ask what may be done for her, whether she would be spoken for to the king or the captain of the host. She answers that she dwells among her own people.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Gehazi tells Elisha the woman has no child and her husband is old. Elisha tells her that about this season, according to the time of life, she shall embrace a son. Like our mother Sarah, she does not believe it and tells the man of God not to lie to his handmaid, yet she conceives and bears a son at that season.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: When the child is grown, he goes out to his father to the reapers and cries, my head, my head. His father has a lad carry him to his mother, and he sits on her knees till noon and then dies, from what seemed only a headache.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: She carries the child up and lays him on the bed of the man of God, the bed in the chamber she had made for Elisha, shuts the door, and goes out. She calls to her husband for a young man and an ass so she may run to the man of God, and though he asks why, since it is neither new moon nor sabbath, she answers, it shall be well.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: She rides to Elisha at Carmel, and when the man of God sees her afar off, he sends Gehazi to ask whether it is well with her, her husband, and the child, and she answers, it is well.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: When she comes to Elisha at the hill, she catches him by the feet, and Gehazi comes near to thrust her away, but the man of God says let her alone, for her soul is vexed within her and the Lord has hid it from him. She says, did I desire a son of my lord, did I not say do not deceive me.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha tells Gehazi to gird up his loins, take his staff, greet no man on the way, and lay the staff on the face of the child. The mother says, as the Lord liveth and as thy soul liveth, I will not leave thee, so Elisha rises and follows her.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Gehazi goes on before them and lays the staff on the face of the child, but there is neither voice nor hearing. He returns to tell Elisha the child is not awake.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: When Elisha comes to the house, the child is dead, laid upon his bed. He goes in, shuts the door upon them both, and prays to the Lord.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: He goes up and lies upon the child, putting his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretches himself upon the child, and the flesh of the child grows warm. He walks in the house to and fro, goes up and stretches himself upon him again, and the child sneezes seven times and opens his eyes.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha calls Gehazi to call the Shunammite, and when she comes he tells her to take up her son. She falls at his feet, bows to the ground, takes up her son, and goes out. This is another act of the Most High through Elisha, restoring the child to life.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha comes again to Gilgal, where there is a dearth in the land, and the sons of the prophets sit before him. He tells his servant to set on the great pot and seethe pottage for them.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: One goes out into the field to gather herbs, finds a wild vine, and gathers his lap full of wild gourds, shredding them into the pot, for they knew them not. As the men eat, they cry out, O thou man of God, there is death in the pot, and they cannot eat.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha tells them to bring meal, casts it into the pot, and says pour out for the people that they may eat, and there is no harm in the pot. He cures the poisoned food so the men may eat safely.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: A man comes from Baal-shalisha and brings the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and full ears of corn in the husk. Elisha says, give to the people that they may eat.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: His servant asks how he should set this before a hundred men, but Elisha says again, give to the people, for thus saith the Lord, they shall eat and shall leave thereof. He sets it before them, and they eat and leave some, according to the word of the Lord.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son
